subject: BrightPlan workspace initiation — invite cascade and API key sequencing
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@brightplan.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: BrightPlan workspace initiation — invite cascade and API key sequencing

Hi Emma —

Welcome aboard, and thanks again for choosing Redwood for inference in BrightPlan’s recommendation pipeline. I’m Ava (CS lead) and I’ll own the initial tenant activation and the invite cascade for your workspace.

Quick plan in three bullets:
- Day 0 (this email): confirm admin roster and sign off on the first admin invite list.
- Day 1: seed admin service keys into the new project namespace and send contributor invites.
- Day 3: handoff to PM for integration run and schedule a 60-minute runbook walkthrough.

Attached is a CSV template for the invite cascade (brightplan-invite-list.csv) and our one-page onboarding checklist (redwood-onboarding-checklist.pdf). Please reply with the CSV filled with the two initial admins and one integration owner (roles: Owner / Admin / Developer).

Notes on API keys: we recommend seeding a long-lived service key scoped to a project namespace for server-side inference and one ephemeral key for developer sandbox. We’ll provide the exact commands in the Day 1 message.

Proposed meeting: Wed, Aug 5, 2026 10:00 AM PT for the runbook walkthrough — does that work for your team?

If you prefer that we create the workspace and invite users directly, confirm the admin emails and we’ll proceed.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: brightplan-invite-list.csv (CSV), redwood-onboarding-checklist.pdf (PDF)

From: Emma Li <emma.li@brightplan.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@brightplan.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightPlan workspace initiation — invite cascade and API key sequencing

Hi Ava —

Thanks — this looks good. We’ll take the Owner/Admin/Developer split. I attached the filled CSV in my reply (see attached list).

Quick answers:
- Admins: emma.li@brightplan.com (Owner), raj.patel@brightplan.com (Admin)
- Integration owner: integrations@brightplan.com (Developer)

The proposed Wed 10:00 AM PT runbook session works for us. If you can seed the service key ahead of time and leave it in a restricted project namespace, that’d be ideal so our infra team can validate connectivity during the call.

Also: are there any required DLP or IP allowlist steps we need to prepare on our side?

—Emma
Emma Li
Head of Data & ML, BrightPlan
emma.li@brightplan.com

Attachments: brightplan-invite-list_filled.csv (CSV)

> Admins: emma.li@brightplan.com (Owner), raj.patel@brightplan.com (Admin)

Nice — I’ll do the project create and key-seed tomorrow morning (Day 1). Ava: plan to share the exact CLI steps and the minimal IAM bindings for the service key.

Checklist for Day 1 (my assignment):
- Create project namespace: brightplan-prod-2026
- Generate service key: scope=project:read,project:invoke (rotate on request)
- Create ephemeral dev key for integrations@brightplan.com
- Add IP allowlist notes in the onboarding doc (Emma: we’ll include the IP ranges we use for hosted endpoints)

I’ll post the CLI snippet in a follow-up and attach the initial service key in our secure vault — we won’t email keys directly.

—Ben

ben.carter@redwood.com

> I’ll do the project create and key-seed tomorrow morning (Day 1). Ava: plan to share the exact CLI steps and the minimal IAM bindings for the service key.

Thanks team — confirming final plan ahead of our runbook walkthrough at 10:00 AM PT today:
- Ben will create brightplan-prod-2026 and seed the service key in the vault.
- I’ll post the CLI + curl examples for validating token auth before the call.
- Marissa will lead the runbook demo and cover telemetry dashboards and cost monitoring.

Emma/Raj: please join the meeting with access to your network admin (for IP allowlist) if possible — we’ll provide the allowlist ranges in the first 15 minutes so your infra team can confirm outbound rules.

Agenda (60 min):
1) Quick intros (5)
2) Project & keys walkthrough (15)
3) Integration test (20)
4) Telemetry + cost controls (10)
5) Next steps & owners (10)

See you shortly.

Ava Chen
